sources.cite: AWS documentation (Amazon EC2 User Guide), Network maximum transmission unit (MTU) for your EC2 instance
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (the AWS China mirror of the user guide page). Relevant text: traffic over VPN connections and through an internet gateway is limited to 1500 bytes; inter-Region VPC peering supports 8500; for IPv4 a device that drops an oversized packet returns 'Destination Unreachable: Fragmentation Needed and Don't Fragment was Set' (Type 3, Code 4) and the sender retransmits smaller; PMTUD responses reach the instance if the security group allows inbound ICMP or the connection is tracked, and 'ICMP can still be blocked by a network ACL that denies ICMP to the subnet'. The companion page 'Set the MTU for your Amazon EC2 instances' (read 2026-11-18) says all current-generation instance types support 9001-byte jumbo frames, and shows tracepath reporting a path MTU that drops to 1500 and ip link show/set for the interface MTU; the case's servers are configured for 9001.

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Brightwell Insurance. Last night the claims reporting servers moved to a VPC subnet reached from the head office over AWS Site-to-Site VPN. This morning logins and small queries work, but any report larger than a page hangs until it times out. The finance close review uses those reports at 10:30.
handover: The reporting instances are current-generation types; nobody changed their network settings.
Last week a hardening ticket replaced the subnet's network ACL with an explicit allow list.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the head office, the VPN, the reporting subnet's network ACL and the reporting servers.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The finance close review starts at 10:30, 80 minutes after the report.

allowicmp.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output: neteng@bastion:~$ aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0c3d --ingress --rule-number 90 --protocol 1 --icmp-type-code Code=4,Type=3 --cidr-block 10.20.0.0/16 --rule-action allow

effects.log: The servers now receive 'fragmentation needed' from the 1500-byte VPN path, cache the smaller path MTU, and resend; large reports complete. Only the one ICMP message type is opened.

effects.log: Reports work, and the claims subnet's network ACL now admits any traffic from anywhere: the hardening control is gone.

writeup.question: For the record: why only large reports hung, what you changed, and how the hardened ACL keeps working.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The servers use a 9001 MTU and the VPN path carries 1500; the hardened network ACL allowed only TCP, so the ICMP type 3 code 4 replies that tell the sender to shrink packets were dropped, and only large responses failed.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Added an inbound ACL rule for ICMP type 3 code 4 from the office range; the path MTU now shows 1500 and the full report runs in seconds. An allow-all ACL would have dropped the hardening; a larger instance changes nothing.

parts.label: Keeps working
parts.modelAnswer: The ACL template carries the PMTUD rule with its reason, and rejected ICMP from the VPN in flow logs alarms.

expertPath.text: MTU 9001, path MTU never learned; ACL allows only TCP; flow logs reject VPN ICMP; SG allows ICMP.
ACL rule for ICMP 3/4; template and alarm.

aclOpened.headline: Open the one message PMTUD needs
aclOpened.body: Path MTU discovery needs ICMP type 3 code 4 to reach the sender. Allowing that message keeps the rest of the allow list.

reviewBlind.headline: Small works, large hangs: think packet size
reviewBlind.body: When handshakes and small replies work but large ones stall, check MTU along the path and whether ICMP fragmentation-needed messages are dropped.

pmtudFixed.headline: Good: a packet-size fault found and fixed narrowly
pmtudFixed.body: You compared the interface MTU with the path, found the network ACL dropping fragmentation-needed messages, allowed only that ICMP type, verified a large report, and fixed the template.

scoring.modelReasoning: Small replies work and large ones hang, so suspect packet size. The servers send 9001-byte packets, the VPN path carries 1500, and the hardened network ACL drops the ICMP fragmentation-needed messages that would tell them to shrink. Allow ICMP type 3 code 4 from the office range and check a large report. An allow-all ACL removes the hardening; a bigger instance changes nothing. Then keep the rule in the template and alarm on rejected ICMP.
